display.text: The number of independent pieces of information remaining after estimated quantities impose constraints. For the one-sample t procedure, df = n − 1 because estimating the mean imposes one constraint.

Greater probability in extreme regions of a distribution than in a comparison distribution; t distributions have heavier tails than the standard normal, especially at low degrees of freedom. Also called fat tails.

A test of H₀: μ = μ₀ when population SD is unknown, using t = (x̄ − μ₀)/(s/√n). Under independent normal observations it has a t null distribution with n − 1 degrees of freedom; large-sample use can be approximate.
Fitting a model too closely to the particular sample, such as by using too many predictors relative to the observations, so its results may generalize poorly.
A sample mean's signed distance from its hypothesized population mean in estimated standard-error units: t = (x̄ − μ₀)/(s/√n). Also called t-score.
